## Explore the Models

The interactive workbench turns the article's diagrams into systems you can
change and challenge. It includes double-pendulum, triple-pendulum, and
bilateral golfer models, with force vectors, moment arrows, energy and power
histories, torque counterfactuals, and parameter perturbations.

The workbench is maintained as an open-source resource in the
[Tools pendulum simulator](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/tree/cefcc1878de11804c44cd7d1d19c0ffcf58fa89e/src/pendulum_simulator).
Its PyQt6 desktop interface and React/Tauri interface read the same
[experiment and glossary catalog](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/blob/cefcc1878de11804c44cd7d1d19c0ffcf58fa89e/src/pendulum_simulator/src/double_pendulum_golf/resources/companion_catalog.json).
The catalog provides shared experiment descriptions and terminology. It does
not establish feature parity or numerical agreement between the interfaces:
the React application also has its own TypeScript simulation code. The
instructions below describe source inspected at Tools commit `cefcc1878`;
they are not a new qualification of every backend or a fresh GUI acceptance run.

::: {.callout-important title="Before You Interpret a Plot"}
Treat interactive results as `exploratory_model_output`, the catalog's declared
scientific status. A shared catalog or manifest helper does not guarantee that
every run exports a complete record. Save the actual model revision, backend,
parameters, units, solver settings and intervention with each result. A plot is
model output, not a measurement of a golfer. Published numerical claims require
their own reproducible study and evidence; neither an animation nor a script
alone validates them.
:::

## Choose a Guided Experiment

Open **Companion Guide** in either interface. Each experiment presents its
hypothesis, observables, steps, interpretation tips, falsifier, and limitations
before you change the model. The shared catalog contains these six entries.
Selecting a guide is not equivalent to loading a fully specified numerical
preset; in the React guide, **Open Model** selects the model type.

| Guided Experiment | What to Vary | What to Inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive Transfer in a Two-Link Chain | Proximal drive and distal torque | Distal acceleration, interaction torque, power, and energy closure |
| Distal-Torque Onset Comparison | Wrist-command onset | Late club speed, actuator work, and sensitivity to the timing grid |
| Three-Link Cascade | Segment geometry and timing | Whether the transfer pattern survives an intermediate segment |
| Two-Hand Force and Equivalent-Couple Mechanism | Hand separation and reaction directions | Net club moment, individual forces, and zero-moment-arm control |
| Pointwise and Forward Zero-Torque Counterfactuals | Intervention definition and cut time | Immediate decomposition versus the altered future trajectory |
| Parameter Robustness and Falsifiability Envelope | Geometry, inertia, damping, and timing | Whether a small plausible perturbation reverses the conclusion |

The desktop **Drift Transfer** diagnostics described below are additional
controls, not two more entries in the shared guide. The searchable glossary defines
terms such as interaction torque, equivalent couple, power, work, mass matrix,
Jacobian, and ZTCF family without requiring the reader to leave the experiment.

## Energy Bounds and Reachable Swings

The **Swing Objective Lab** compares five objectives under a shared torque
budget. Its historical 0.50 kg tip-mass example reported nearly stationary hands
at impact; changing the represented club inertia produced substantially higher
terminal hand speeds. These are configuration-dependent simulation reports,
with reference-band and reproducibility limits described in
[When a Double Pendulum's Energy Optimum Stops Its Hands](impact-optimality-and-model-limits.html).

The exact zero-hand-rate result applies to an instantaneous fixed-pose,
fixed-energy problem with collinear links, a point mass at the head, and
positive proximal inertia. It does not require every torque-constrained swing
to stop its hands or reverse the hub torque. Matching one club inertia also
does not preserve its full dynamics.

Compare complete trajectories, all constraints, numerical convergence, and
independently defined measurements before interpreting an objective ordering.
Similar endpoint scores cannot identify which objective a golfer uses. The
linked review corrects the earlier structural and human-inference claims;
it does not certify a new run of the workbench.

## What Would Count Against the Mechanism?

An instantaneous intervention holds the complete state fixed and changes a
declared input. For an affine model, $\dot{x}=f(x)+G(x)u$, its immediate effect is
$G(x)(u_1-u_0)$. A forward intervention starts from the same cut state and then
evolves a different trajectory. The later difference includes both the changed
input and the changed state; it is not generally the original pointwise input
term. Specify whether activation, passive elasticity, damping and contact remain
in the counterfactual. Removing a commanded joint torque need not remove stored
energy or turn muscles off.

Predeclare the observable, interval, constraints and expected effect size.
Unchanged distal acceleration at one instant is not a universal falsifier:
symmetry, cancellation or the selected output can make the immediate difference
zero. A credible challenge is failure of a *specified nonzero prediction* under
matched conditions and declared numerical uncertainty. Other useful checks are:

- a timing advantage that disappears under matched initial states or reverses
  under a plausible parameter change, narrowing its claimed robustness;
- an implementation that disagrees with an independently derived force or
  power balance for the same model and boundary; or
- an apparent effect that fails step-size refinement or depends on an
  unreported force, impulse, constraint or energy source.

For the two-hand check, let $\mathbf f_R,\mathbf f_L$ be forces exerted by the
hands **on the club**, define $\mathbf d=\mathbf r_R-\mathbf r_L$, and take
moments about the midpoint. Express all vectors in the same frame. The resultant is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf F&=\mathbf f_R+\mathbf f_L,\\
\mathbf M_{\mathrm{mid}}&=
\frac{\mathbf d}{2}\times(\mathbf f_R-\mathbf f_L)\\
&\quad+\mathbf m_R+\mathbf m_L.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\mathbf m_R,\mathbf m_L$ are contact moments applied directly to the club.
Coincident hands eliminate the separated-force contribution for bounded forces;
they need not eliminate those contact moments or the resultant force's moment
about another point. Equal and opposite forces form a pure couple; a general
two-hand wrench also has a net force. This follows the declared-point
[wrench convention](https://modernrobotics.northwestern.edu/nu-gm-book-resource/3-4-wrenches/).
Distinguish an implementation check, a model prediction and a test in people.

## Run It Locally

For the source version described here, create a fresh checkout of
[D-sorganization/Tools](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools.git
cd Tools
git checkout cefcc1878de11804c44cd7d1d19c0ffcf58fa89e
```

Use an activated virtual environment with Python 3.11 or later for the desktop
installation. Record resolved dependency versions as well as the source commit;
an editable install does not freeze dependencies.

### PyQt6 Desktop Interface

```bash
# From the Tools repository root:
python -m pip install -e ".[gui]" -e src/pendulum_simulator
python -m double_pendulum_golf
```

The root package supplies shared GUI modules used by the simulator; installing
only the nested simulator package omits that part of the source dependency.

After a double-pendulum run, open the docked **Analysis** panel and select the
**Drift Transfer** tab. Choose the start and end of the phase to inspect. The
tab reports distal kinetic-energy gain, drift and control grip work, Negative Grip
Work, wrist-control work, peak grip force, and peak distal speed, while plotting
the power and speed histories. Its displayed proximal-link angular velocity is
not an anatomical shoulder or torso measurement. The tab accepts the
double-pendulum result type; it does not provide this analysis for the other
model tiers. At the inspected revision, window summaries use saved samples
inside the requested interval without interpolating its endpoints. Use saved
sample times when specifying an exact integration window.

For supported double-pendulum runs, the same panel includes
**Full-Trajectory Coordinate Force Sources**. It reports
signed and absolute tangent impulse and generalized work under the shared `force-attribution/v1`
contract. The Christoffel split uses shoulder-absolute and wrist-relative
coordinates. It is a modeled equation-term attribution, not a measured muscle
force, and unsupported friction, clamp, or joint-limit terms fail closed rather
than being folded into another source. These source summaries cover the full
trajectory, while the transfer summary uses the selected window. Coordinate
terms can change under reparameterization; they are not independently measured
physical agencies. An undefined tangent-force allocation is not a zero force.

### Read Work and Energy With the Same Model

Grip-force power is $P_F=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v_{\mathrm{grip}}$, using force
on the club and the velocity of its material point at the grip interface;
its integral has units of joules. Tangent impulse has units of newton-seconds and cannot be
substituted for work. Where grip speed is zero, the motion tangent is undefined,
although force power is well defined and zero. Negative Grip Work integrates
the negative portion of force power, rather than classifying it from force sign.

A moment acting **on the club** contributes
$P_M=\mathbf m\cdot\boldsymbol\omega_{\mathrm{club}}$. The net power of an
equal-and-opposite actuator moment pair uses the **relative** angular velocity
of the two bodies. These are different system boundaries. To check a club's
kinetic-energy change, include gravity work and every other external force and
moment. If gravitational potential is included in the energy, do not count
gravity work again. Damping, impacts and compliance require their own terms.

::: {.callout-important title="A Known Diagnostic Consistency Limit"}
At the pinned revision, the Python fallback
[`mass_matrix`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/blob/cefcc1878de11804c44cd7d1d19c0ffcf58fa89e/src/pendulum_simulator/src/double_pendulum_golf/physics.py)
places shaft mass $m_2$ together with clubhead mass $m_c$ at the distal tip.
The transfer diagnostic's
[`_club_kinetic_energy`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/blob/cefcc1878de11804c44cd7d1d19c0ffcf58fa89e/src/pendulum_simulator/src/double_pendulum_golf/transfer_strategy.py)
instead treats the shaft as a uniform rod. With the proximal link instantaneously
stationary and club angular rate $\omega$, they give, respectively,

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{\mathrm{tip}}&=\tfrac12(m_2+m_c)L_2^2\omega^2,\\
T_{\mathrm{rod}}&=\tfrac12(m_2/3+m_c)L_2^2\omega^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

For $m_2=3\,\mathrm{kg}$, $m_c=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $L_2=1\,\mathrm m$ and
$\omega=2\,\mathrm{rad/s}$, the same state yields 8 J versus 4 J. These are
illustrative test parameters, not a golf-club specification. A transfer-energy
comparison must reconcile this mass-distribution mismatch first. This source
check does not qualify native or TypeScript backends.

Moreover, the reported work-closure residual is
$W_{\mathrm{total}}-W_{\mathrm{drift}}-W_{\mathrm{control}}$ on the same
trajectory. Because control force is constructed as total minus drift, a small
residual checks the additive split and integration; it does **not** check
$\Delta T$ against external work. Do not use it as evidence that the full
energy budget closes.
:::

### React/Tauri Interface

```bash
# From the Tools repository root:
cd src/pendulum_simulator/pendulum-web
npm ci
npm run dev
# Or launch the native desktop wrapper:
npm run tauri dev
```

The native wrapper additionally requires Rust and the platform dependencies in
the [Tauri prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/).

Developers using UpstreamDrift can also open the **Pendulum Simulator** tile.
The launcher resolves the sibling Tools provider and its dockable adapter; it
does not maintain a second physics implementation.

## A Productive Review Sequence

1. Read the hypothesis and falsifier before running the experiment.
2. Record the actual starting state, parameters, units, backend and numerical
   settings; a guide title does not supply them.
3. Inspect vectors and signed power, not animation alone.
4. Run the matched counterfactual and negative control.
5. Perturb geometry, inertia, damping, timing, and numerical step size.
6. Record observations that weaken the interpretation as carefully as those
   that support it.
7. Promote a result to the scientific resource only through a deterministic
   script, frozen inputs, convergence and closure tests, and machine-readable
   output. Resolve the diagnostic consistency limit above before interpreting
   transfer-energy closure.

## Interpretation Boundary

The models illuminate mechanics under declared assumptions. They do not by
themselves identify muscle action, scapular coordination, tissue slack, a
preferred swing strategy, or a universal route to clubhead speed. A generalized
torque is not a muscle, an interaction force is not voluntary effort, and a
negative torque is not necessarily negative biological work.

Choose human measurements to distinguish the specific competing explanations.
Bilateral hand wrenches and club kinematics constrain interface power; ground
reactions help close a whole-body balance; activation or stiffness hypotheses
need additional observations and a calibrated observation model. No single
universal sensor list identifies every mechanism, and activation recordings
alone do not directly measure muscle force. The
[governed technical monograph](proximal_distal_energy_transfer/index.html)
specifies those evidence boundaries and links the deterministic studies behind
the article. Its models, claims, and evidence are pinned to
[UpstreamDrift commit `85cce4d3`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/85cce4d3307bb7ad3953d9fc6e583e370803515c/docs/research/proximal_distal_energy_transfer).
That versioned computational baseline does not establish validation in human golfers.

Return to [_How a Golf Swing Carries Energy_](proximal-distal-a-journey-through-the-swing.html)
for the visual narrative, read the
[technical summary](proximal-distal-energy-transfer.html) for a shorter synthesis,
or use the [technical monograph](proximal_distal_energy_transfer/index.html) for the
full mathematical and evidentiary treatment.
